beats.intro: Learning module four. [[sub]]How arbitrage and replication pin down the price of a forward.
beats.lawone: [[head]]Arbitrage is a riskless profit. It appears when the law of one price fails. [[bonds]]Two identical zero-coupon bonds both pay one hundred euros at maturity. Bond A costs ninety-nine. Bond B costs ninety-nine fifteen. [[t0]]Today, buy A and sell B short. You collect fifteen cents. [[tT]]At maturity, A pays one hundred, which covers the one hundred you owe on B. Nothing is left to pay. [[profit]]The fifteen cents is a riskless profit. [[conv]]As traders do this, B's price falls and A's rises, until they are equal.
beats.pvrule: [[head]]The second rule: an asset with a known future price must trade at that price, discounted at the risk-free rate. [[setup]]Gold trades at seventeen seventy today. Procam can sell it forward in three months at seventeen ninety-two thirteen. The risk-free rate is two percent. [[t0]]Procam borrows seventeen seventy and buys gold, and sells it forward. Its net cash today is zero. [[tT]]In three months, it delivers the gold for seventeen ninety-two thirteen, and repays the loan with interest: seventeen seventy-eight seventy-eight. [[profit]]That leaves thirteen dollars thirty-five an ounce, with no risk. [[why]]The spot price was too low. Discounted, the forward price is worth seventeen eighty-three twenty-eight today.
beats.rule: [[curve]]So with no income or costs, the forward price is the spot price grown at the risk-free rate: F sub zero of T equals S sub zero, times one plus r, to the power T. [[rate]]A higher rate widens the gap between forward and spot. [[time]]So does a longer time to maturity. [[repo]]In practice, the relevant risk-free rate is the repo rate. [[neg]]And if rates are negative, the forward price is below the spot price.
beats.replicate: [[head]]Replication recreates a derivative's cash flows with the underlying and borrowing or lending. Now gold is priced fairly: spot seventeen eighty-three twenty-eight. [[fwd]]Path one: a long forward at seventeen ninety-two thirteen. No cash today. At maturity, S sub T minus the forward price. [[rep]]Path two: borrow seventeen eighty-three twenty-eight and buy the gold. Again, no cash today. [[repT]]At maturity, sell the gold at S sub T, and repay seventeen eighty-three twenty-eight grown at two percent, which is exactly seventeen ninety-two thirteen. [[same]]Both paths pay S sub T minus seventeen ninety-two thirteen. [[sc]]If gold goes to nineteen hundred, both make ten thousand seven hundred eighty-seven dollars on a hundred ounces. If it falls to seventeen hundred, both lose nine thousand two hundred thirteen.
beats.hedge: [[long]]Now combine a long gold position, [[short]]with a short forward. [[flat]]The two lines cancel. The profit is the same whatever gold does: the forward price minus the spot price. [[rate]]Procam pays one hundred seventy-eight thousand three hundred twenty-eight today, and receives one hundred seventy-nine thousand two hundred thirteen in three months. That return is exactly two percent, the risk-free rate. A fully hedged position earns the risk-free rate.
beats.carry: [[head]]Owning an asset has other costs and benefits. Together with the risk-free rate, they make up the cost of carry. [[cost]]Costs, such as storage and insurance for commodities, raise the forward price. [[ben]]Benefits, such as dividends or coupons, lower it, because the forward buyer does not receive them. [[f1]]With known amounts, the forward price is the spot price, minus the present value of income, plus the present value of costs, all grown at the risk-free rate. [[f2]]With rates, under continuous compounding, the exponent is r plus c minus i, times T. [[tab]]If costs exceed benefits, the forward is above spot. If benefits are larger, it is below.
beats.dividend: [[head]]An equity forward. Unilever trades at fifty euros, the rate is five percent, and the forward is for six months. [[nodiv]]With no dividend, the forward price is fifty times one point oh five to the power one half: fifty-one twenty-three. [[div]]Now Unilever pays thirty cents in three months, and again at six months. [[pv]]Their present value is fifty-eight point nine two cents. [[f]]Subtract it from the spot price, then grow at five percent: the forward price is fifty point six three one. [[gap]]The dividends shrink the gap between forward and spot from one twenty-three to about sixty-three cents.
beats.index: [[head]]For an index, the dividend is a yield, so we use continuous compounding. [[data]]The NIFTY fifty is at fifteen thousand two hundred. The rupee risk-free rate is four percent, and the dividend yield two point two percent. [[f]]The forward for three months is fifteen thousand two hundred, times e to the power of four percent minus two point two percent, times one quarter. [[ans]]That is fifteen thousand two hundred sixty-eight point five five.
beats.fx: [[head]]For currencies, each side has its own interest rate. The spot rate is one point three three three five Australian dollars per U S dollar. [[rates]]Six-month rates: point oh five percent in Australian dollars, point two percent in U S dollars. [[s1]]Borrow one thousand U S dollars, [[s2]]convert them to one thousand three hundred thirty-three Australian dollars fifty, [[s3]]and lend those at the Australian rate. [[s4]]In six months you receive one thousand three hundred thirty-three eighty-three Australian dollars, [[s5]]and owe one thousand and one U S dollars. [[f]]The only fair forward rate makes these equal: one point three three two five. [[eq]]In general, the forward is the spot times e to the power of the foreign rate minus the domestic rate, times T.
beats.fxrule: [[head]]So the interest rate differential decides the forward. [[pos]]If the price currency's rate is higher, the forward is above spot, and that currency trades at a forward discount. [[neg]]If its rate is lower, as with the Australian dollar, the forward is below spot: a forward premium. [[mon]]For Montau, the spot rate is thirteen hundred won per euro, with won rates at point seven five percent and euro rates at minus point two five. [[ans]]The seventy-five day forward is thirteen hundred two point six seven. The won trades at a forward discount.
beats.commodity: [[head]]Commodities carry physical costs. Add storage and insurance of two dollars an ounce, paid at the end of three months. [[pv]]Its present value is one dollar ninety-nine. [[f]]The forward price rises to seventeen eighty-three twenty-eight plus one ninety-nine, grown at two percent: seventeen ninety-four thirteen. [[cy]]Sometimes owning the physical good itself has value, for example when inventories are low. That non-cash benefit is a convenience yield. [[low]]It can push forward prices well below the no-arbitrage level.
beats.wrap: [[w1]]Arbitrage forces identical cash flows to have the same price. [[w2]]A forward can be replicated by borrowing and buying the underlying, so F sub zero equals S sub zero times one plus r to the T. [[w3]]Costs raise the forward price; income and convenience yield lower it. [[w4]]For currencies, the interest rate differential sets the forward rate.
beats.finish: That's the end of learning module four.
